name: S Vineeth Kumar
deck: Five farmers, five acres, four harvests of Napier grass. Seasonal crops on that land return around forty-five thousand rupees an acre a year. This is the trial that asks whether biomass beats it.
description: Five farmers, five acres and four harvests of Napier grass in Chikaballapura, plus the variety trials that named Pangong-3 the one worth planting.

aims.p: Napier grass as a crop with a buyer, not fodder nobody sells. What it yields, what it costs to keep, and who pays for it.

aims.h: Find the variety that actually yields
aims.p: Trials across varieties put Pangong-3 super Napier at the top, with a daily harvesting routine written down behind it so the next farmer does not start from scratch.

did: Ran awareness sessions with farmers around Chinthamani
Piloted cultivation with five farmers on about five acres
Took four harvest cycles off the pilot plots
Mapped land layout and irrigation and monitored soil through the cycles
Trialled varieties and settled on Pangong-3 super Napier as the highest yielding
Wrote daily harvesting procedures and began digestibility tests on the feedstock for biogas

figures.label: Biomass harvested
figures.note: The report gives this as an approximate figure.

quotes.text: We were unsure in the beginning, but after seeing multiple harvests, we now believe this crop can give steady income.
quotes.speaker: A farmer on the pilot plots

quotes.text: Napier grass grows well on our land and requires less replanting compared to seasonal crops.
quotes.speaker: A farmer on the pilot plots

holes: This one has no end. It started on 10 February 2025, a year ahead of the rest of the cohort, and the report calls it ongoing.
Both farmer testimonials arrive without a name, so there is nobody to go back to for a second question.
Two of the three objectives were left blank in the report. What is here is the first one.
